strengths: The paper addresses an important problem: unreliable minority-class pseudo-labels in semi-supervised graph learning. Examining representation geometry provides a useful perspective on this failure mode.

UNREAL is modular and applicable to several GNN backbones. The reported evaluation spans synthetic and natural imbalance, with substantial improvements in several settings. For example, Table 20 reports Cora/GCN Macro-F1 of 76.44 versus 72.67 for the strongest baseline at imbalance ratio 10.

The extensive appendices include pseudo-label accuracy analyses, sensitivity studies, pseudocode, hyperparameter ranges, and hardware details. Repeated experiments and a public code link support reproducibility. No material research-ethics concern is apparent from the reported work.
weaknesses: Theorem 1 is not valid as stated. Even with two vMF classes, moving an embedding toward the wrong class center can increase geometric imbalance while decreasing prediction entropy. Appendix C also gives contradictory bounds: when D_intra=0, they require H >= log C and H <= log C - κ/(2C²). These problems undermine the central theoretical contribution.

Theorem 2 does not establish the claimed dependence on labeled class imbalance. Subsampling labels on a fixed graph changes ρ without changing neighborhood class composition; with a fixed encoder and class centers, geometric imbalance need not increase. Appendix D assumes the required relationship between ρ and cross-class neighbor influence without a graph-generation model, then inconsistently changes a claimed ρ² dependence into ρ.

The connection between the analyzed quantity and the implemented filtering rule is insufficiently established. Definition 1 measures distance to the true class center relative to global class separation, whereas DGIS uses the nearest and second-nearest centroids. A node near an incorrect centroid can pass DGIS despite substantial true-class deviation. No bound or direct validation establishes that this surrogate approximates the formal score.

Theorem 3 establishes an algebraic weighting property, not a reduction in geometric imbalance or pseudo-label error. Moreover, the confidence coefficient min(r,1-r) decreases once r exceeds 0.5, so the claimed progressive increase in confidence influence is not generally guaranteed by the proposed formula.

The ablation reporting is internally inconsistent. As printed, Tables 1 and 32 mark NR and DGIS as disabled in the highlighted best-performing rows, contradicting the claim that their combination explains the strongest results. Corrected component indicators and corresponding results are necessary to assess the method's individual contributions. Claims of uniform superiority also overlook reported losses, including Computers-Random with SAGE in Table 4.

The methodological novelty needs clearer differentiation from prior work. DPAM closely resembles the clustering/classifier agreement mechanism of M3S, acknowledged in Appendix B, but the direct M3S comparison is limited to CS-Random. IceBerg, a directly relevant cited 2025 self-training method, is not evaluated. Broader matched comparisons would better establish the contribution beyond existing pseudo-label alignment.

The efficiency claims lack end-to-end support. Appendix K considers up to 100 self-training rounds with up to 2000 epochs per round, while Table 12 reports fixed-epoch training and isolated selection timings. Full-run runtime and memory comparisons under comparable training budgets are needed. Reproduction is also hindered by limited configuration details for the added large-scale experiments and inconsistent descriptions of error bars as standard errors versus standard deviations.
